Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `main` @ `a485b9217858da95d56230526fc1af9d02b26bc4`. The issue has no integration-branch metadata, so there is no mismatch to check.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _run_security_audit
Scope-mode justification: The failure is in the test harness, not in the product. `_run_security_audit` in `tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py` copies the runner's environment and strips only `AI_ENGINE*` and `CLAUDE_*` keys (lines 247-251). On a CI pull-request job, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` points at the real PR payload. When a test does not set `AI_ENGINE_LABELS`, `scripts/claude_engine.py::work_item_labels` (lines 330-355) reads the labels from that payload, and labels take precedence over `AI_ENGINE_SECURITY_AUDIT`. So the PR's own labels can pick the engine that a test expected to pin. `tests/test_claude_engine.py::_run` (line 39) and `tests/test_ai_engine.py` (line 130) already strip `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` for this reason. The fix adds the same strip to the existing filter. Per the Boil the Lake rule, I also include a small regression test (well under 30 LOC) so the leak cannot come back silently. That follows §6 Core Priorities in `unattended_system_instructions.md` (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed): completeness moves correctness. Production engine precedence stays the same.

## Files likely to change

1. `tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py`, the only file the triage lists.
2. Only if CLAUDE.md §20 requires an entry for test-only changes: `changelog.d/6757-security-audit-test-event-path.md`. This is a one-line fragment under "Fixed" and is not shown to users.

No changes to `scripts/security_audit.sh`, `scripts/claude_engine.py`, `scripts/ai_engine.sh`, or any workflow YAML. A search confirmed that `security_audit.sh`, `ai_engine.sh` and `security-audit.yml` never read `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` themselves. Only `claude_engine.py` does, so removing it from the test environment affects nothing except engine label resolution.

## Functions or modules to implement

1. `_run_security_audit` (around lines 249-251). Widen the existing engine-isolation filter:
   - From: `env = {k: v for k, v in env.items() if not k.startswith(("AI_ENGINE", "CLAUDE_"))}`
   - To: also exclude the key `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`.
   - Update the comment: "Engine selection must not leak in from the caller's environment (CI jobs carry a real GITHUB_EVENT_PATH whose PR labels would override AI_ENGINE_SECURITY_AUDIT)."
   - Keep the filter before `env.update(...)` and before any `extra_env` merge. A test that deliberately passes `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` or `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` in `extra_env` must still win. The explicit `AI_ENGINE_LABELS='["ai:codex"]'` case in `test_security_audit_codex_engine_or_codex_label_never_starts_claude` must keep working unchanged.
2. `test_security_audit_codex_engine_or_codex_label_never_starts_claude` (around lines 2722-2727). Make the existing `assert "security-audit: engine=codex" in proc.stdout` print its context on failure, using `proc.stderr` (which already contains `AI_ENGINE_SELECTED ... source=`). This changes diagnostics only, not semantics.
3. New regression test `test_security_audit_ignores_inherited_event_path_labels`. Check the name is unique in the file first.
   - Write a temporary event payload: `{"pull_request": {"labels": [{"name": "ai:engine-claude"}]}}`.
   - Temporarily set `os.environ["GITHUB_EVENT_PATH"]` to that file with try/finally, restoring or popping the previous value afterwards.
   - Run `_claude_engine_audit(Path(td), claude_env={"AI_ENGINE_SECURITY_AUDIT": "codex"})`.
   - Assert `returncode == 0`, `"security-audit: engine=codex"` in stdout, no `claude_calls`, and kept ids `["codex-finding"]`.
   - Before the fix this test fails, because the inherited label selects Claude. After the fix it passes.
   - Check how this file is executed. CI runs `python3 tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py` (ci.yml line 766), so if the file has a `__main__` runner that lists tests explicitly, register the new test there too. Otherwise pytest-style discovery of `test_*` functions is enough.

## Data structures affected

Only the subprocess environment dict built by the test helper. No state files, schemas or markers change.

## API or interface changes

None. Production engine precedence (labels > `AI_ENGINE_<ROLE>` > `AI_ENGINE` > config default) is intentionally left alone.

## Decisions

### D1 — Strip GITHUB_EVENT_PATH in the shared test helper instead of per test
- Chosen: add `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` to the existing environment filter in `_run_security_audit`.
- Alternatives considered: set `AI_ENGINE_LABELS=""` in every engine test (setting it, even empty, short-circuits payload reads); change `claude_engine.py` precedence; stop the CI job from exporting the event path.
- Why: a single change covers every caller, including Claude-path tests such as `test_security_audit_role_default_runs_claude`, which could be broken the same way by an `ai:codex` PR label. It matches the precedent in `tests/test_claude_engine.py` and `tests/test_ai_engine.py`, and leaves production behavior as it is.

### D2 — Add a regression test that reproduces the leak
- Chosen: a test that injects a label-bearing `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` into the parent environment and asserts the codex pin still holds.
- Alternatives considered: rely on CI labels to catch a regression.
- Why: the failure only appears when a PR carries an engine label, so without a deterministic reproduction it would come and go depending on labels. The test costs well under 30 LOC.

## Security considerations

- Trust boundaries: none touched. This is a test-only change. The PR event payload is CI-controlled data that should never influence hermetic tests.
- Authorization: there are no new endpoints or surfaces.
- External-input validation: unchanged. Production `work_item_labels` still reads the payload in real jobs.
- Abuse cases: none introduced. Not changing production precedence means the `ai:codex` and `ai:engine-claude` labels still route real audits as documented. The regression test writes its temporary payload only under a temp directory.

## Risks and edge cases

- The `os.environ` mutation in the regression test must be restored in `finally`. Otherwise later tests in the same process would inherit the fake payload. Since the helper now strips the key, a leak would be harmless, but restore it anyway.
- Some test in this file may intentionally rely on the inherited `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`. A grep found no references in the file, so none appear to. Any such test can still pass the key via `extra_env`, which is applied after the filter.
- The triage did not confirm the PR's labels, so the root cause is likely but unconfirmed. The fix is correct either way: it removes a real source of non-determinism. The added stderr context will show `source=` if the test ever fails again for a different reason.
- Conflict detection: no conflicts. The cited line ranges (247-251, 2722-2727) and `claude_engine.py` 330-355 match the current ref.

## Testing considerations

- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py`, the same invocation CI uses.
- Run it again with `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` exported to a payload labelled `ai:engine-claude`, to simulate the CI condition. Every test should pass.
- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py -q`, if pytest is available, and `ruff check tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py`.
- The final authority is the `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` job and the aggregate `CI / lint` on the fix PR. PR #6752 can be re-run after merge.

## Pre-execution self-check

- Every claim is grounded in code read on this ref: the helper filter, the failing test, `work_item_labels`, and the existing precedent in two other test files.
- The scope is limited to one test file plus an optional changelog fragment. No production or workflow edits, no new scripts, no scheduler wiring, and no DB work, so the §20 items do not apply.
- Assumption: whether CLAUDE.md §20 requires a changelog fragment for a test-only fix is left to the implementer. Add `changelog.d/6757-security-audit-test-event-path.md` only if it does.
